speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with a limp and localized pain, correct? Can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and how it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis. 

The clinical presentation of a limp and localized pain in the left knee of a 7-year-old male, without fever or trauma, is highly suggestive of transient synovitis. However, given the age and location, it is also important to rule out Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease or an occult femoral neck fracture. 

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP. 
REQUEST IMAGES: Anteroposterior and Lateral X-Ray of the Left Hip.
